directChecks.method: Sum hypot(dx,dy) for adjacent wire points on the same layer; ignore duplicate zero-length points and zero-planar-length layer transfers. Distinct trace objects are counted separately, so overlapping same-net copper can be double-counted.

directChecks.formula: 45 degree lower bound = max(abs(dx),abs(dy)) + (sqrt(2)-1)*min(abs(dx),abs(dy)); bounds omit obstacles, layer transfer cost and specified isolation.

directChecks.check: Do not let short local stubs hide long-trace economy

directChecks.interpretation: 166 of 433 vias serve GND; total via count alone cannot establish wasted vias.

strengths: Most geometry is close to the shortest permissible 45° geometry: median 1.00× and weighted total 1.141× before obstacles.
95 routes longer than 10 mm retain a weighted 1.191× 45° ratio; useful evidence of reasonable economy beyond short stubs.
The longest debug LED trunk is essentially a shortest 45° path; a long line is not necessarily badly routed.
Separate fan current and Kelvin/sense paths have legitimate engineering reasons to avoid the visually shortest connection.

findings.explanation: Confirmed 90.59 mm peripheral fan-supply route is the largest length penalty (50.57 mm beyond the obstacle-free 45° bound). The source explicitly separates fan current from the quiet ADC tap, so isolation is justified. The right-edge excursion to x=48.8 mm remains a candidate to shorten while preserving that separation; no collision-free alternative was established. A large ratio alone is not a short or mandatory reroute.

Confirmed UART TX route goes east to x=19.375 mm then south to y=-33.4 mm before returning west to its header. Its 56.08 mm route has 23.17 mm excess over the 45° geometric bound. Worth optimizing jointly with UART RX/header placement; a shorter clearance-valid route is an unproven candidate.

Confirmed input-fault pull-up makes a broad eastward excursion to x=-9.25 mm despite endpoints only 2.25 mm apart in x. Fourteen nonzero segments and 30.24 mm length versus a 14.63 mm 45° bound show substantial detour. This low-current control route is not a thermal concern, but it consumes inner-layer space; obstacle avoidance may justify it.

Confirmed raw logic-supply route is 68.96 mm and uses two layer transfers versus a 45.71 mm geometric 45° lower bound. Separate raw-supply branch and bounded internal load are stated design intentions. Re-evaluate placement/corridor with local regulator decoupling retained; the current path is not proven unsafe.

The longest individual trace is 91.29 mm, but its endpoints are 88.26 mm apart and its 45° bound is also 91.29 mm. This is efficient route geometry, not a routing detour. Its cost arises from the centralized indicator placement spanning the board; local LED placement could reduce future congestion if the user interface permits.

suspectedShortAssessment.classification: Not independently established by this economy review
suspectedShortAssessment.explanation: Viewed the user crop. It does not provide net labels or layer identity, and I have not located its copper against the circuit geometry; therefore no short/no-short conclusion follows from the image. Net-aware copper/clearance specialist review is required. Efficiency findings above do not prove a foreign-net overlap.

topImprovements: First investigate a shorter protected fan-supply corridor preserving quiet ADC and Kelvin isolation; it dominates geometric excess.
Co-optimize UART TX/RX routes and header placement instead of accepting separate large detours.
Simplify the INPUT_FAULT_N pull-up corridor if a net-aware clearance audit can prove a shorter alternative.
Consider local LEDs in a future placement pass; centralized debug indicators force otherwise efficient long board-spanning routes.
limitations: Read-only review; no replacement path was routed or checked against all pads, pours and barrels.
Metrics are sums of trace-object centerlines, not unique copper length or extracted parasitics.
Geometric lower bounds omit real obstacles, current-return behavior, controlled impedance and transfer constraints; they are opportunity indicators rather than safe replacement lengths.
This role did not conduct complete foreign-net short/clearance DRC and makes no manufacturing or bench readiness claim.
Overall static score 7.4/10 is from routing economy alone; a confirmed short from another reviewer would override this provisional score.
